title: Game: Jelly Shift
description:
## Jelly Shift — Complete Game Implementation

Implement the Jelly Shift game at src/games/jelly-shift/. Auto-runner where players reshape a jelly blob to fit through wall holes.

### Files to Create
- src/games/jelly-shift/index.html — standalone entry point with meta tags, loading shell
- src/games/jelly-shift/state.js — pure functions: advance(state, dt) with speed escalation, reshape(state, widthDelta) preserving area (height=1/width, clamp [0.3, 3.0]), checkWallCollision(state, wallIdx), fitsHole(blobWidth, blobHeight, hole)
- src/games/jelly-shift/renderer.js — Three.js: tunnel corridor geometry, soft-body blob mesh (sphere with vertex displacement driven by width/height, translucent MeshPhysicalMaterial with transmission), solid gray wall planes with colored hole cutouts (stencil masks), pass squish animation + particle burst, fail splat + screen shake
- src/games/jelly-shift/input.js — drag/swipe vertically: up = tall+narrow, down = wide+flat; continuous real-time control
- src/games/jelly-shift/game.js — lifecycle integration with Three.js RAF loop and Cannon-es soft-body (if needed)
- src/games/jelly-shift/generator.js — place walls at decreasing z-intervals, alternate tall/wide/compound shapes, verify achievable within [0.3, 3.0] range, ensure consecutive transitions are achievable given reshape speed
- src/games/jelly-shift/levels.json — 15 levels with escalating wall frequency and compound shapes
- src/games/jelly-shift/styles.css

### Key Logic
- Blob area preservation: width * height = 1.0 (approximately)
- Simple shapes (tall/wide): check blob.width <= hole.width AND blob.height <= hole.height
- Compound shapes (plus): check blob fits within union of horizontal and vertical rectangles
- Speed escalates over time
- Landscape orientation (844x390 logical)

### Tests to Create
- tests/solvers/jelly-shift-solver.js — geometric feasibility per wall: compute valid width range, verify overlap with [0.3, 3.0], verify transition time between consecutive walls
- tests/unit/jelly-shift.test.js — fitsHole true/false, reshape clamps, reshape preserves area, speed escalation
- tests/e2e/jelly-shift.spec.js — blob renders in corridor, reshape to match wall = pass, wrong shape = splat animation

### Validation
- Every level: all walls passable (solver geometric check)
- Every level: consecutive wall transitions achievable (reshape time budget)
- Most complex rendering in the project (soft-body deformation, compound holes)

### References
- Plan: /home/coding/mobile-gaming/docs/implementation/plan.md (lines 1266-1339)

title: Asset Pipeline (Procedural Graphics, Audio, Icons)
description:
## Asset Pipeline (Procedural Graphics, Audio, Icons)

All visual and audio assets are procedural — zero bitmap files in the repo.

### Implementation
- 2D games: Canvas path operations (beginPath, arc, moveTo, lineTo, fill, stroke)
  - shared/shapes.js: drawRoundedRect, drawCircleWithHighlight, drawArrow, drawTube, etc.
  - Each game's renderer.js composes primitives into game-specific visuals
  - Colors from shared/colors.js palette (never hardcoded hex)
- 3D games: Three.js built-in geometries (CapsuleGeometry, BoxGeometry, SphereGeometry, etc.)
  - MeshStandardMaterial for solid, MeshPhysicalMaterial with transmission for Jelly Shift
  - No external model files (.glb, .obj) — everything programmatic
  - InstancedMesh for crowds, collectibles, block piles
- Sound: Web Audio API oscillators and noise generators
  - shared/audio.js sound presets as parameter objects
  - Per-game sounds: pop, whoosh, crunch, sparkle, thud
  - No audio file dependencies (< 2KB of JS)
- Icons: scripts/generate-icons.js renders public/favicon.svg to 192px + 512px PNG via sharp
- OG images: Playwright-generated 1200x630 PNGs committed to public/og/

### Acceptance Criteria
- Zero bitmap files in repo (except committed OG images)
- All graphics render correctly from code
- All sounds synthesized via Web Audio API
- Icons generate correctly at 192px and 512px
- OG images render each game's initial state

### References
- Plan: /home/coding/mobile-gaming/docs/implementation/plan.md (lines 1689-1713)

title: Pull the Pin shows empty canvas — game.js not loading after deploy fix
description:
## Bug
Pull the Pin game at https://mobile-gaming.pages.dev/pull-the-pin/ renders the HTML shell (header, footer, canvas element) but the canvas is empty — no game logic runs.

## Likely Cause
The `src/games/pull-the-pin/index.html` loads `<script type="module" src="game.js">` with a relative path. After the `flattenSrcOutput` Vite plugin moves the built HTML from `dist/src/games/pull-the-pin/` to `dist/pull-the-pin/`, the relative `game.js` reference may not resolve correctly. Vite should bundle the script into `/assets/` with a hashed name, but may not be processing the entry correctly for game pages (vs the hub which works).

Check:
1. Compare the built `dist/pull-the-pin/index.html` — does it have a bundled script tag or still reference `game.js`?
2. Check if ALL game pages have the same issue (not just pull-the-pin)
3. The hub works because its entry is explicitly listed; game entries may need different handling in the Vite input config

## Repro
Visit https://mobile-gaming.pages.dev/pull-the-pin/ — canvas is blank, no interactivity.

## Context
Introduced by the deploy fix commits (flatten Vite output plugin). The game HTML, CSS, and structure load fine; only the JS game logic fails to execute.

comments.author: coding
comments.text: Confirmed: affects ALL game pages, not just pull-the-pin. Built HTML only includes modulepreload polyfill - no game script bundle. Hub works correctly. Root cause: Vite is not resolving the relative game.js script tags in game HTML into bundles.

## Goal
Transform flat grid puzzle into a charming bus stop scene.

## Current State
Canvas 2D with gray roads, green grass, colored buses with windows, passenger stick figures, green exit glow, path preview dashed line, smooth movement with ease-out quad.

- **Bus character:** Round bus corners more, add headlights/taillights, window reflections, cartoon personality

- **Boarding satisfaction:** Satisfying click/snap when passenger boards matching bus, brief color flash
- **Departure animation:** Bus drives away with exhaust puff particle, smooth acceleration curve
- **Street atmosphere:** Add sidewalk texture, simple building silhouettes in background, subtle street details

title: Design Your Own Ad Compositor
description:
## "Design Your Own Ad" Compositor (7.2)

LOW PRIORITY. Template-driven tool to turn gameplay recordings into fake mobile game ads.

### Files to Create
- src/shared/ad-compositor.js — template engine, segment sequencing, overlay rendering, MP4 export

### Implementation
- 5 templates:
  - Fail Ad: 2 wrong moves, cut before resolution, "NO!" text, dramatic zoom
  - Challenge Ad: "Only 1% can solve this!", IQ percentage, timer, emoji reactions
  - Satisfying Ad: loop most satisfying 3 seconds, slow-motion, ASMR audio
  - Drama Ad: dramatic pause, wrong answer, red X, sad trombone
  - Speedrun Ad: 4x speed with timer, abrupt stop, "Can you beat 4.2s?"
- Template definition as JSON: segments (gameplay/black/outro), overlays (text/qr with triggers)
- Compositor: seek through recorded buffer, apply speed changes, draw overlays, encode MP4
- UX: level complete -> "Create an Ad?" -> template picker -> 3s render -> preview -> edit text -> export
- QR code in outro links back to playable game (viral loop)

### Tests
- Unit: template segments sequence correctly
- Unit: overlay triggers fire at correct timestamps
- E2E: template picker renders, export produces video

### Acceptance Criteria
- 5 templates produce visually distinct ad-style videos
- QR code in video links to playable game
- Export produces shareable MP4
- Custom text overlay editing works

### Dependencies
- Phase 6.5 video recording infrastructure
- Gameplay recording buffer

### References
- Plan: /home/coding/mobile-gaming/docs/implementation/plan.md (lines 2332-2382)

title: Phase 6: Power Features
description:
## Phase 6: Power Features

Features that transform the game collection from standalone toys into a shareable, social, self-adjusting platform.

### Tasks
1. State URLs (6.1) — Encode game state in URL hash via pako compression
2. Solver-Powered Hints (6.2) — In-game hint system using existing solvers
3. Daily Challenge (6.3) — One seeded level per game per day, share cards
4. Quick Play (6.4) — One-tap game selection based on play history
5. Video Recording (6.5) — Canvas capture, WebM/MP4 encoding, social sharing
6. Deterministic Replays (6.6) — Input sequence recording and playback
7. Fail Speedrun (6.7) — Race to trigger fail state, "Ad Recreation" badge
8. Swipe Navigation (6.8) — Swipe between games without returning to hub
9. Adaptive Difficulty (6.9) — Frustration-aware silent difficulty adjustment

### Prerequisites
- Phase 0 storage for 6.1, 6.4, 6.9
- Game solvers from Phases 1-3 for 6.2, 6.3
- Phase 5 polish for 6.5
- >= 3 games complete for 6.4
- >= 2 games complete for 6.8

### References
- Plan: /home/coding/mobile-gaming/docs/implementation/plan.md (lines 1829-2265)

title: Zero-Friction Quick Play
description:
## Zero-Friction Quick Play (6.4)

One tap -> playing. Intelligent game selection based on play history.

### Files to Create
- src/shared/quick-play.js — pickGame() algorithm

### Implementation
- pickGame() reads localStorage play history: gameId, lastPlayed, levelsCompleted, avgSolveTime, retryRate
- Scoring: recencyPenalty + varietyBonus + difficultyMatch
  - recencyPenalty: games played in last hour score lower
  - varietyBonus: never-played games score highest
  - difficultyMatch: 10-30% retry rate scores highest (flow zone)
- Select highest-scoring game, pick next unsolved level at current difficulty tier
- Hub integration: large "Quick Play" button above game grid
- Preload top-2 candidates via <link rel="modulepreload"> on hub load
- Fallback (first visit): Water Sort level 1

### Tests
- Unit: pickGame with various play histories returns expected game
- Unit: recency penalty, variety bonus, difficulty match scoring
- E2E: Quick Play button on hub, tapping loads a game

### Acceptance Criteria
- Quick Play selects appropriate game based on history
- First-time visitors get Water Sort level 1
- Transition is near-instant due to preloading
- No game selection or level selection screens

### Dependencies
- Phase 0 storage
- >= 3 games complete

title: Game: Satisfying/ASMR
description:
## Satisfying/ASMR — Complete Game Implementation

Implement the Satisfying/ASMR game at src/games/satisfying/. Primary subtype: Pressure Washing — drag to spray clean a dirty surface. No fail state.

### Files to Create
- src/games/satisfying/index.html — standalone entry point with meta tags, loading shell
- src/games/satisfying/state.js — pure functions: initDirtMap(width, height, pattern, density), spray(state, x, y), calculateCleanPercent(dirtMap), checkComplete(state). State serialization via sprayLog (ordered spray coordinates) instead of raw dirtMap Uint8Array.
- src/games/satisfying/renderer.js — Canvas 2D: two-layer canvas (bottom=clean surface color, top=dirt overlay), spray erases dirt pixels to reveal clean surface, water droplet particle effects from nozzle
- src/games/satisfying/input.js — touch/mouse down = nozzle active, continuous drag = continuous spray, up = nozzle inactive
- src/games/satisfying/game.js — lifecycle integration
- src/games/satisfying/generator.js — procedural dirt patterns: full, splatter (random patches), stripes
- src/games/satisfying/levels.json — 10 levels with varying patterns, densities, nozzle radii
- src/games/satisfying/audio.js — synthesized water-spray sound (white noise through bandpass filter)
- src/games/satisfying/styles.css

### Additional Subtypes (variants within same game)
- Bubble Pop: grid of bubbles, tap to pop, all popped = complete
- Soap Cutting: drag blade across soap block, each slice reveals cross-section

### Key Logic
- dirtMap is 300x400 Uint8Array (255=dirty, 0=clean)
- spray() clears pixels within nozzleRadius
- cleanThreshold (default 0.95) triggers completion
- No fail state — game cannot be lost
- State serialized as sprayLog for URLs/storage (not raw dirtMap)

### Tests to Create
- tests/solvers/satisfying-solver.js — systematic grid scan (left-to-right, top-to-bottom, stride=nozzleRadius)
- tests/unit/satisfying.test.js — spray clears pixels within radius, calculateCleanPercent correct ratio, checkComplete triggers at threshold, dirt patterns generate expected density
- tests/e2e/satisfying.spec.js — dirt surface renders, drag creates clean trail, systematic drag triggers completion

### Validation
- Every level completable via systematic scan solver
- Nozzle radius large enough that scan completes within 5000 spray operations

### References
- Plan: /home/coding/mobile-gaming/docs/implementation/plan.md (lines 933-1011)

title: Game: Makeover Run
description:
## Makeover Run — Complete Game Implementation

Implement the Makeover Run game at src/games/makeover-run/. Auto-runner where players steer through upgrade/downgrade stations, then get a star rating at the end.

### Files to Create
- src/games/makeover-run/index.html — standalone entry point with meta tags, loading shell
- src/games/makeover-run/state.js — pure functions: advance(state, dt), hitStation(state, stationIdx) for upgrades (set category to max(current, upgrade)) and downgrades (reduce by amount, floor 0), startJudging(state), judge(state) returning 1-3 stars based on score/maxScore, steer(state, xDelta)
- src/games/makeover-run/renderer.js — Three.js: runway corridor, articulated character mesh with swappable parts (hair, outfit, accessory meshes changing in real-time), archway gate stations with icons (scissors, dress, lipstick, mud), gold/sparkle aura for positive, dark/mud for negative, end judging pose + star rating panel
- src/games/makeover-run/input.js — swipe/drag left-right to steer; auto-runner forward
- src/games/makeover-run/game.js — lifecycle integration with Three.js RAF loop
- src/games/makeover-run/generator.js — place station pairs at z-intervals (one positive, one negative or two positive different types), verify max score = 3 stars, min score <= 1 star, 60% positive hits = 2 stars
- src/games/makeover-run/levels.json — 15 levels with varying station layouts
- src/games/makeover-run/styles.css

### Key Logic
- 4 appearance categories: hair, outfit, makeup, accessories (each 0-3)
- maxScore = 12 (3 per category x 4)
- Positive stations only upgrade, never downgrade a better state
- Judging: <33% = 1 star, 33-66% = 2 stars, 67-100% = 3 stars
- Landscape orientation (844x390 logical)

### Tests to Create
- tests/solvers/makeover-run-solver.js — optimal path (all positive, avoid all negative), worst path (all negative), average path (random steering)
- tests/unit/makeover-run.test.js — hitStation positive/negative, judge star boundaries, appearance values clamped 0-3
- tests/e2e/makeover-run.spec.js — character renders in "before" state, positive station visual transformation, judging overlay with stars

### Validation
- Every level: optimal path -> 3 stars
- Every level: worst path -> <= 1 star
- No two stations at same z and same x

### References
- Plan: /home/coding/mobile-gaming/docs/implementation/plan.md (lines 1342-1421)

Original Save the Girl uses pencil-drawing style with narrative engagement. Simplicity is intentional but character reactions drive emotional investment.

description:
## Hub JavaScript: Game Card Rendering and Quick Play

Implement hub.js with dynamic game card rendering, filtering, and Quick Play functionality.

### Files to Create/Modify
- `src/hub/hub.js` — game card rendering and interaction logic

### What to Implement
- Game registry: array of game objects with { slug, title, description, category, thumbnailColor }
- `renderGameCards(container, games)`: populate #game-grid with game cards, including "Play" links
- `filterGames(category)`: show/hide cards by category (all, puzzle, interactive, runner)
- Quick Play handler: `#quick-play` click -> redirect to random game's first level
- Daily challenge handler: `#daily-challenge` click -> redirect to today's seeded challenge URL (derive game+level from `Date.now()` day seed)
- Export functions for testability

### Test Command
```bash
test -f src/hub/hub.js && node -e "const fs = require('fs'); const code = fs.readFileSync('src/hub/hub.js','utf8'); if (!code.includes('renderGameCards') || !code.includes('quick-play')) process.exit(1);" ; echo "EXIT: $?"
```

### Pass/Fail Criteria
- src/hub/hub.js exists
- Contains renderGameCards function that populates game grid
- Contains Quick Play click handler targeting #quick-play

description:
## Save the Character: Solver and Unit/E2E Tests

Implement the automated solver and all test suites for Save the Character.

### Files to Create
- `tests/solvers/save-the-character-solver.js` — automated solver
- `tests/unit/save-the-character.test.js` — unit tests for state.js
- `tests/e2e/save-the-character.spec.js` — end-to-end browser tests

### What to Implement in solver
- Load levels.json, for each scenario:
  - Find the choice with `correct: true`
  - Call `selectChoice(state, correctChoiceId)` then `resolveChoice(state)`
  - Assert final status === "won"
- Also verify every non-correct choice results in "lost"
- Exit 0 if all pass, exit 1 with details on failure

### What to Implement in unit tests (vitest)
- Test createInitialState returns correct shape
- Test selectChoice with correct choice ID sets selectedChoice and status "animating"
- Test selectChoice with incorrect choice ID sets selectedChoice and status "animating"
- Test resolveChoice after correct selection -> status "won"
- Test resolveChoice after incorrect selection -> status "lost"
- Test every scenario has exactly one correct choice (iterate levels.json)
- Test selectChoice is pure (input state not mutated)

### What to Implement in e2e tests (playwright)
- Test: game loads and choice buttons are visible on canvas
- Test: clicking wrong choice shows failure animation
- Test: clicking correct choice shows celebration animation
- Test: game advances to next level after correct choice

### Test Command
```bash
npx vitest run tests/unit/save-the-character.test.js && node tests/solvers/save-the-character-solver.js; echo "EXIT: $?"
```

### Pass/Fail Criteria
- Solver passes all 20 scenarios (correct choice -> won, each wrong choice -> lost)
- Unit tests: all state function tests pass
- Unit tests: all 20 scenarios validated (exactly one correct choice each)
- E2E tests: game loads and renders choice buttons

title: Fail Speedrun Mode
description:
## Fail Speedrun Mode (6.7)

Race to trigger the fail state as fast as possible — mirrors the fake-ad phenomenon.

### Files to Create
- src/shared/fail-speedrun.js — mode activation, per-game fail objectives, timer, leaderboard

### Implementation
- Activation: toggle in game settings or swipe-up on level-complete screen
- Per-game fail objectives:
  - Pull the Pin: first ball into wrong cup (fastest pin pull)
  - Water Sort: pour wrong color (fastest wrong pour)
  - Parking Escape: fewest moves to return to initial state (undo speedrun)
  - Brain Teaser: tap most obvious wrong answer (fastest wrong tap)
  - Save the Character: pick worst choice (fastest tap)
  - Merge Games: fill grid completely (fastest overflow)
  - Crowd Runner: reduce crowd to minimum before boss (lowest arrival count)
  - Giant Runner: arrive at boss smallest possible (lowest scale)
  - Bridge Race: let all opponents finish first (last place speedrun)
  - Jelly Shift: splat on first wall (fastest splat)
  - Makeover Run: hit every negative station (lowest score)
  - Satisfying/ASMR: excluded (no fail state)
- Millisecond-precision timer: starts on first input, stops on fail
- Personal best leaderboard per level in localStorage
- "Ad Recreation" badge: fail in under 3s on Pull the Pin or Save the Character

### Tests
- Unit: fail objectives trigger correctly per game
- Unit: timer precision
- E2E: fail speedrun mode activates, timer runs, fail triggers end

### Acceptance Criteria
- Fail speedrun available for 10 of 12 games
- Timer starts on first input, stops on fail state
- Personal best tracked in localStorage
- "Ad Recreation" badge awarded correctly

### Dependencies

title: Game: Merge Games — 2D grid merge puzzle
description:
Phase 2 2D Interactive game using Canvas 2D.

## State Model
```
{ grid: 2D array (null or {tier, chain}), gridWidth: 7, gridHeight: 7, tasks: [{chain, tier, count}], spawnTimer, bonusChance: 0.05 }
```

## Mechanics
- Drag matching items (same tier + same chain) to merge -> tier+1
- 5% bonus chance -> tier+2
- Gravity drops items after merge
- Chain reactions cascade
- Complete tasks by collecting required tier items

## Chains
- wood (brown), stone (gray), iron (silver), gold (yellow), diamond (cyan)
- Tier 1-5 within each chain

## Renderer
- Canvas 2D grid with item sprites
- Merge pulse animation, cascade sparkle, task progress bar

## Input
- Drag item to adjacent cell with matching tier+chain

## Solver
- Greedy merge-all simulation — verify all tasks reachable from initial grid

## Generator
- Seed grid with low-tier items + define tasks requiring higher tiers
- Verify solvable

## Levels
- 15 hand-crafted with increasing task complexity

## Files
- src/games/merge/{state.js, renderer.js, input.js, game.js, generator.js, levels.json, index.html}

- Merge logic, gravity cascade, task completion, solver, E2E

- src/games/parking-escape/index.html — standalone entry point
- src/games/parking-escape/state.js — pure functions: buildOccupancyGrid(), getValidMoves(), moveVehicle(), checkWin(), undo(), getAllValidMoves()

- src/games/parking-escape/styles.css

### Key Logic
- Vehicles slide only along their orientation axis (horizontal=left/right, vertical=up/down)
- Occupancy grid prevents overlapping moves

- Move count tracking with undo support

  1. Read difficulty tier from adaptive difficulty (6.9)
  2. Map tier to generator parameters (e.g., Water Sort tier 1 = 4 colors 2 buffers, tier 10 = 8 colors 1 buffer)
  3. Call generator.js with sequential seed: createRng(sessionSeed + levelIndex)
  4. Solver-verify solvability and difficulty metrics
  5. If solver fails: increment seed, retry (max 5 attempts, then relax constraints)
  6. Cache in memory (ephemeral, not localStorage)
- Applicable games (10 of 12): Water Sort, Parking Escape, Pull the Pin, Merge, Crowd Runner, Giant Runner, Jelly Shift, Makeover Run, Bridge Race, Satisfying/ASMR
- Excluded: Brain Teaser, Save the Character (hand-crafted only)
- Scoring: levels completed = primary, streak multiplier (x1.0->x1.2->x1.5->x2.0, resets on hint)
- Personal best in localStorage
- Difficulty ratchet: every 5 levels, tier +1 (independent of adaptive)
- Session end: 3 retries on same level (puzzle) or loss (runner)
- "Continue?" option: restart level but streak resets to x1.0
- Shareable: session score + level count + game type as share card

### Tests
- Unit: tier-to-parameter mapping produces valid generator inputs
- Unit: sequential seeds produce different but deterministic levels
- Unit: scoring with streak multiplier
- Integration: 50 generated levels per tier all solvable

### Acceptance Criteria
- Endless mode available for 10 games after hand-crafted levels exhausted
- Generated levels are always solvable
- Difficulty ratchets up every 5 levels
- Session scoring with streak multiplier works
- Personal bests tracked

### Dependencies
- Generators + solvers from Phases 1-3
- Adaptive difficulty (6.9)

### References

title: Graphics polish: Satisfying ASMR — material rendering and tactile feel
description:
## Goal
Transform flat dirt-clearing into a tactile material experience.

## Current State
Tan/beige clean surface, brown dirt overlay grid, circular erase with radius falloff, offscreen canvas. Minimal visual engagement.

## Improvements
- **Material variety:** Add different material types (soap, sand, slime) with distinct visual properties
- **Translucency:** Semi-transparent materials that reveal layers underneath
- **Texture detail:** Subtle noise/grain texture instead of flat colors
- **Particle debris:** Small particles fly off when erasing/cutting — dust, crumbs, shavings
- **Haptic sync points:** Mark interaction points for haptic feedback integration
- **Color layers:** Hidden color patterns revealed by erasing (satisfying reveal mechanic)
- **Tool variety:** Different erase shapes (knife slice, brush sweep, pressure wash)
- **Smooth interaction:** Erase should follow finger with slight trail/smear effect
- **Completion sparkle:** Satisfying shimmer/sparkle when fully cleaned

## Reference
Original ASMR games use semi-realistic 3D rendering with translucency, glitter, layered colors. The tactile simulation is the core appeal.

title: Game: Crowd Runner
description:
## Crowd Runner — Complete Game Implementation

Implement the Crowd Runner game at src/games/crowd-runner/. Auto-runner where players steer a crowd through math gates to grow or shrink, then fight a boss at the end.

### Files to Create
- src/games/crowd-runner/index.html — standalone entry point with meta tags, loading shell
- src/games/crowd-runner/state.js — pure functions: advance(state, dt), crossGate(state, gate, side), hitBoss(state), steer(state, direction). Gate operations: +, -, x, / with floor at 1.
- src/games/crowd-runner/renderer.js — Three.js: flat textured course plane, instanced mesh crowd (capsule/sphere geometry scaling with count), colored gate arches with text meshes, large instanced boss cluster, chase camera. Win: boss explodes into particles. Lose: crowd scatters.
- src/games/crowd-runner/input.js — swipe/drag left-right to steer between lanes; auto-runner forward motion
- src/games/crowd-runner/game.js — lifecycle integration with Three.js RAF loop
- src/games/crowd-runner/generator.js — place gates at z-intervals with good/bad options, calculate optimal/worst paths, size boss to ~80% of optimal crowd
- src/games/crowd-runner/levels.json — 20 levels across difficulty tiers
- src/games/crowd-runner/styles.css

### Key Logic
- laneOffset < 0 = left gate, >= 0 = right gate
- Gate operations: + (add), - (subtract, floor 1), x (multiply), / (divide+floor, floor 1)
- Boss fight: crowdSize > boss.size = won, else lost
- Landscape orientation (844x390 logical)

### Tests to Create
- tests/solvers/crowd-runner-solver.js — exhaustive 2^N gate combinations (N<=10), find optimal/worst paths, verify at least one path beats boss and at least one loses
- tests/unit/crowd-runner.test.js — crossGate operations, floor at 1, hitBoss comparison, gate side from laneOffset
- tests/e2e/crowd-runner.spec.js — crowd renders with starting count, good gates increase count, win/loss result

### Validation
- Every level: optimal path beats boss by >= 20% margin
- Every level: at least one path loses
- Generated levels: 50 per difficulty, all solvable, boss within margin

### References
- Plan: /home/coding/mobile-gaming/docs/implementation/plan.md (lines 1020-1114)
